chunks: ʿUmar ibn Yazīd asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام:
About an Imam with whom there is no problem in all of his affairs, knowledgeable, except that he makes his parents hear harsh speech that angers them—should I recite behind him?
He said: “No. Recite behind him so long as he is not undutiful and one who severs ties.”

key_terms.أَبَوَيْهِ: his two parents, whose rights are central in the question
key_terms.إِمَامٍ: the prayer leader being evaluated for congregational salat
key_terms.الْكَلَامَ الْغَلِيظَ: harsh or severe speech that causes hurt
key_terms.تَقْرَأُ خَلْفَهُ: to recite behind him in congregational prayer
key_terms.عَارِفٍ: possessing knowledge and recognition in religious matters
key_terms.يَغِيظُهُمَا: it angers or distresses the two parents

ai.seo_question: Can one pray behind an Imam who speaks harshly to his parents?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the ruling of praying behind an Imam whose general conduct and knowledge are sound, but who speaks harshly to his parents. It indicates that such behavior is blameworthy, yet prayer behind him is not barred unless he reaches the level of being openly undutiful and severing kinship ties.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1113 - Umar ibn Yazid asked Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as)

about an Imam who is generally good in all his affairs and knowledgeable, but he raises his voice and speaks harshly to his parents, causing them distress.
He asked: "Should I pray behind him?"
He (as) replied: "No, do not pray behind him as long as he is not openly defiant and severing ties”.
